newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINES DOWNSCALES FOREIGN REMITTANCE TARGETS.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINES DOWNSCALES FOREIGN REMITTANCE TARGETS.

text.p: The Philippines has scaled down its targets for foreign exchange remittances from Filipinos working abroad, a government data released on Thursday said.
The Philippines relies heavily on remittances from overseas Filipinos to bring up its gross national product.

Based on the document, inflows from investment and personal income from Filipinos living abroad will be lower at $6.728 billion this year from the original target of $7.448 billion but higher than the 1996 level of $5.996 billion.
Outflows from investment expenses and personal income will increase to $2.980 billion from an earlier estimate of $2.946 billion.
A department of finance official said the lower contribution from overseas Filipinos is a healthy sign that the domestic economy is providing quality employment opportunities for the Filipinos.
At present, there are 6.5 million Filipino overseas workers.
The official did not say how the lower remittances will affect the gross national product.
